query: For a high-entropy alloy coating system on a transition metal matrix, what is the relationship between ambient temperature and tribological performance? Please hypothesize the dominant mechanism linking thermal conditions to wear resistance and propose a boundary where performance degrades.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy alloy (HEA) coatings on transition metal matrices, tribological performance initially improves with moderate ambient temperature increases (up to ~300°C) due to the formation of a protective tribo-oxide layer that reduces friction and wear. However, beyond a critical temperature threshold (~300-400°C), performance degrades significantly due to excessive tribochemical reactions, oxide layer instability, and increased adhesion wear, leading to a sharp rise in the coefficient of friction and wear rate.
generation.material_initial_state: Nanocrystalline refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) coating (e.g., CuMoTaWV) deposited on a 304 stainless-steel transition metal matrix, with grain size ~18 nm and high hardness (~19 GPa).
generation.intervention: Exposure to varying ambient temperatures during sliding contact against a steel counterface (e.g., E52100 alloy steel) under constant load (1 N).
generation.conditions: Atmospheric environment, sliding distance up to 15 m, temperatures ranging from room temperature (RT) to 300°C and above.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation and evolution of a tribo-oxide layer (e.g., CuO, MoO3, WO3) and changes in surface roughness and adhesion properties.
generation.mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the HEA coating forms a stable, protective oxide layer that acts as a solid lubricant, reducing friction and wear. As temperature increases beyond the threshold, the oxide layer becomes unstable, leading to excessive tribochemical reactions, increased adhesion, and plastic deformation, which drastically increases friction and wear rates.
generation.predicted_outcome: Wear rate and coefficient of friction (COF) will show a minimum at moderate temperatures (~300°C) and increase sharply at higher temperatures (>300°C). Specifically, COF may rise from ~0.25 at RT to ~1.5 at 300°C due to tribochemical reactions, and wear rate may increase from ~6.4e-6 mm³/N·m at RT to ~2.5e-5 mm³/N·m at 300°C.
generation.baseline: Room temperature wear behavior of the as-deposited or annealed HEA coating, characterized by low friction and wear rates due to the inherent hardness and nanocrystalline structure of the alloy.
generation.boundary: The performance degradation boundary is estimated to be around 300-400°C, beyond which the protective oxide layer becomes unstable and tribochemical reactions dominate, leading to rapid wear and increased friction.
generation.uncertainty: The exact temperature threshold for performance degradation may vary depending on the specific HEA composition, coating microstructure, and environmental conditions (e.g., humidity, oxygen partial pressure). The observed behavior in CuMoTaWV may not generalize to all HEA systems without further validation.
generation.falsification_experiment: Conduct wear tests on the same HEA coating system at temperatures ranging from RT to 500°C in controlled atmospheres (air, inert gas). Measure COF and wear rate at each temperature. If the wear rate and COF do not show a minimum at ~300°C and a sharp increase at higher temperatures, the hypothesis is falsified. Additionally, analyze the wear track composition and morphology using EDS and SEM to confirm the presence and stability of the tribo-oxide layer.

Abstract In this study, the wear behaviour of a powder metallurgically produced AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 high-entropy alloy (HEAs) is investigated at elevated temperatures. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of inert gas atomised feedstock enables the production of dense bulk material. The microstructure evolution and phase formation are analysed. The high cooling rate in the atomisation process results in spherical powder with a microstructure comprising two finely distributed body-centred cubic phases. An additional phase with a complex crystal structure precipitates during SPS processing, while no coarsening of microstructural features occurs. The wear resistance under reciprocating wear conditions increases at elevated temperatures due to the formation of a protective oxide layer under atmospherical conditions. Additionally, the coefficient of friction (COF) slightly decreases with increasing temperature. SPS processing is suitable for the production of HEA bulk material. An increase in the wear resistance at elevated temperature enables high temperature applications of the HEA system AlCoCrFeNiTi 0.5 .
